tips.text: Be specific about the output format and the constraints. If you want more than the bare task, say so.
Give the context a new coworker would need: who it is for, and what done looks like.
Show an example of the output you want, in the format you want it back.
Put a long document in XML tags so the instruction and the source stay separate.
Give Claude a role when the job needs a point of view, such as a careful editor.
Say how long the answer should be, and ask it to skip the preamble if you only want the result.
Put standing instructions, such as tone and a correct example, where they outrank the one-off request.
Separate identity, instructions, and examples instead of one undifferentiated block.
Markdown and XML both work for marking off sections of a long prompt.
Include the context the answer depends on, instead of assuming the model already has it.
Say the format, the length, and what to leave out. Current models follow specific instructions.
Keep a copy of a prompt that worked. Behavior can change when the model changes.
Say whether the input is a question, a task to perform, or text to finish.
State the constraints: how long, what to include, and what to leave out.
Name the response format, such as a list or a table.
Add a few examples when the format is easy to miss, and keep those examples in one format.
Add the background the answer needs before you ask for it.
Break a large job into parts instead of one crowded instruction.
